sections.title: Eligibility and preparation
sections.text:
Eligibility for your route [Standing rule]
U.S. bachelor’s before enrollment is an eligible degree route; UChicago mathematics preparation is relevant.
GPA and full degree timing must be checked. International applicants are explicitly accepted. [s4] [s1]
Before submission [Conflict]
Complete BOTH Graduate School application and separate Department Background and Interest Form. The
linked form is still labeled Fall 2026: obtain current-cycle confirmation before using it. If inaccessible,
department asks contact before December 18 (year not stated). [s1] [s3]
Adviser contact [Standing rule]
No adviser secured beforehand required; admitted to program then select later. Optional faculty interests on
course list; admissions contact grad@math.uga.edu. [s7] [s1]
Portal workflow [Conflict]
Graduate application plus separate form; upload course list and statement, electronic referees. Current
background form link is stale. [s1] [s3]
Cycle verification [Conflict]
Standing admission rules; mandatory linked supplement explicitly Fall 2026, so Fall 2027 form must be
confirmed. FY 27 salary data are not the 2027-28 offer. [s1] [s3] [s8]

sections.title: English and GRE
sections.text:
English requirement [Standing rule]
TOEFL before Jan 21, 2026:80 overall,20 speaking/writing; after Jan 22:4.5 overall,4 speaking/writing. IELTS 6.5
overall,6 each. TOEFL Home/MyBest/Paper and IELTS Online/One Skill Retake accepted. No Duolingo. Official
agency reporting required; two-year validity. [s5] [s4]
UChicago English exemption [Standing rule]
Completed accredited U.S. degree usually waives testing. Currently enrolled UChicago applicant with at least
one U.S. academic year and strong performance (example GPA≥3.0) may receive waiver. Department can
override; teaching English rules are separate. Confirm waiver rather than infer from F-1 status. [s5] [s4]
GRE General; GRE Mathematics [Standing rule]
Not required; voluntarily reported scores considered. The prior-cycle supplemental form explicitly applies this
to both general and mathematics tests and TA consideration. [s1] [s3]

sections.title: Academic records
sections.text:
Transcripts and degree records [Standing rule]
Upload one unofficial transcript copy; course list required separately. Official-final transcript logistics should be
checked in Graduate School instructions. [s1]
Mathematics-course list [Standing rule]
Required upload: all college math courses, separated by institution and degree; course number/name, actual
grade and textbook if known; mark graduate courses taken as undergraduate with an asterisk. Include
separate undergraduate/graduate math GPAs on 4.0 scale to two decimals. Optional term/year, credits,
in-progress courses. At top give interests and possible faculty; name atop each document, PDF preferred,
US-Letter rather than A4. No length limit published. [s2]
Course descriptions [Unresolved]
Course list explicitly requests titles/textbooks, not full course descriptions; separate description upload
permission unverified. [s2]

sections.title: Funding and fees
sections.text:
Amount and coverage [Unresolved]
Exact mathematics stipend not established. FY 27 university full-time doctoral base is $66,980, NOT the
part-time assistant stipend; do not quote it as an offer. Eligible student-only health subsidy rises to 60%;
assistant tuition reduced to$25/semester, activity fees remain. [s8] [s10]
Years of support [Standing rule]
Department promises five years full support to all PhD students; exact offer conditions/annual stipend must be
obtained. [s1]
International eligibility [Standing rule]
Department’s all-PhD support statement and international application route indicate inclusion; confirm
individual award and TA English eligibility. [s1] [s5]
Conditions and duties [Standing rule]
Assistantships at most 20 hours/week total; full-time enrollment generally 12 credits fall/spring,9 summer.
Teaching English qualification remains separate from admissions waiver. [s9] [s5]
Extra funding application [Standing rule]
Department background form is mandatory in addition to general application; no separate ordinary-TA essay
established. [s1]
Other funding routes [Unresolved]
Competitive grant-funded applied-math research assistantships advertised; may not fit pure algebra/geometry
interests. Graduate School fellowships/department nominations require confirmation. [s1]

Application fee [Standing rule]
$75 first application; $25 additional applications (up to two) and eligible reapplication within one year.
Nonrefundable, due at submission. [s6]
Fee waiver [Standing rule]
Math department says it cannot waive fee. Graduate School only lists qualifying-program exemptions with
documentation in application; eligibility cannot be assumed from international UChicago enrollment. [s6] [s7]

sections.title: Potential advisers and recent research
sections.text:
Algebraic / arithmetic geometry
Valery Alexeev
Moduli and compactification of algebraic surfaces, K3/Enriques surfaces, and log Calabi-Yau geometry. [faculty1]
David C. Barrow Professor; availability unconfirmed.
Research evidence: 2025 · The KSBA moduli space of stable log Calabi-Yau surfaces
Official publication evidence for the stated research match.
Dino Lorenzini
Arithmetic geometry of curves and surfaces, wild quotient singularities, reduction, and arithmetic of number
fields. [faculty2] [faculty2a]
Distinguished Research Professor; official home page explicitly welcomes prospective-group inquiries.
Research evidence: 2025 preprint · Intersection matrices of wild cyclic quotient singularities
Official publication evidence for the stated research match.
William Graham
Equivariant K-theory/intersection theory, flag and Schubert varieties, and geometric representation theory.
[faculty4]
Current faculty; new PhD supervision availability unconfirmed.
Research evidence: 2023 preprint listed on current page · Geometric and combinatorial properties of extended Springer fibers
Official publication evidence for the stated research match.
Number theory
Paul Pollack
Elementary and analytic number theory, multiplicative arithmetic, and arithmetic of quadratic number fields.
[faculty5] [faculty5a]
Professor and Director of Graduate Studies; availability unconfirmed.

Research evidence: 2025 · Maximally elastic quadratic fields
Official publication evidence for the stated research match.
Representation theory
Daniel K. Nakano
Algebraic/quantum groups and Lie superalgebras; cohomology, support varieties, and tensor-triangular
geometry. [faculty7]
Distinguished Research Professor; availability unconfirmed.
Research evidence: 2026 · The homological spectrum and nilpotence theorems for Lie superalgebra representations
Official publication evidence for the stated research match.
